records.issue_text: [BUG] Calling prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany with an empty data object throws a Prisma validation error, so getAvailability crashes on every cache-refresh path. Prisma updateMany with `data: {}` fails validation ("Argument data must provide at least one field") or produces an invalid UPDATE with no SET clause; every Google Calendar availability fetch that reaches this line (i.e., every cache-miss fetch for a Google credential) throws, breaking booking availability for Google users.
records.rationale: The diff adds `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` in `CalendarService.ts`, and `updateManyByCredentialId` directly forwards `data` into `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data })`. Passing an empty object literal as `data` is visible in the diff and is very likely to trigger Prisma validation/runtime failure (updateMany requires at least one field to update), which would crash this code path.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The access-denied / not-found branch throws a plain Error instead of a TRPCError, so an unauthorized or stale credentialId returns an INTERNAL_ERROR (500) rather than a 4xx the tRPC contract implies. A user whose credential was deleted (or passing another user's credentialId) gets a 500 with generic 'Error deleting cache' toast and noise in error monitoring, instead of a clean NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN.
records.rationale: In the newly added `deleteCacheHandler` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts), the unauthorized/not-found case does `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` when the credential isn’t found for `{ id: credentialId, userId: user.id }`. In a tRPC mutation this will typically surface as an `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`/500 rather than a contract-appropriate 4xx (`TRPCError` with `NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN`), matching the finding’s concern about stale/unauthorized `credentialId` producing noisy 500s and only the generic UI toast.

Because expired rows are only cleaned lazily (or never, since deleteManyByCredential is a manual action), the Cache Status shown in the dropdown reports a "last updated" timestamp for a credential whose cached entries are all expired, so users see a status that misrepresents the actual cache state.
records.rationale: `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups by `credentialId` and returns `_max.updatedAt` with only `where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds } }`, with no filter on `expiresAt` (even though `CalendarCache` has an `expiresAt` column). records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `sed -i '' -E` uses the macOS-only empty-suffix form; on GNU/Linux sed this fails with "extra characters at the end of h command", so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated on Linux. Any developer on Linux running the script hits a sed error after the tunnel is already up and the .env write is skipped, leaving a stale webhook URL that makes the subsequent webhook test silently target the old host.
records.rationale: The new script `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` uses `sed -i '' -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|...|" "$ENV_FILE"` (see the added `sed -i '' -E ...` line). The `-i ''` empty-suffix form is BSD/macOS sed-specific; on GNU/Linux sed, `-i` does not accept the empty suffix as a separate argument, so this invocation fails and the env file update is skipped, leaving `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` stale for Linux users.
